keyVerseText: Saying, Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name? and, behold, ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and intend to bring this man's blood upon us.
rootMeaning: The word παραγγελία (parangelía) derives from the verb παραγγέλλω (parangéllō), which means to give a charge or command, or to transmit a message with authority. This etymology highlights the action of delivering an authoritative instruction or mandate, emphasizing not just any communication but one that carries binding force. Unlike a general statement, παραγγελία involves a deliberate ordering or enjoining, reflecting the seriousness and urgency of the message conveyed.
usageInScripture: Παραγγελία appears five times in the New Testament, consistently conveying the sense of a command, charge, or set of instructions. The top translations—such as 'we straitly,' 'a charge,' 'commandments,' and 'of the commandment'—demonstrate its use in contexts where authoritative direction is given, whether in moral teaching or legal summons. This range shows the word’s flexibility in describing both formal orders and moral imperatives, underscoring its role in conveying authoritative guidance from God or human authorities.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding παραγγελία as a command or charge rooted in authoritative transmission deepens our grasp of biblical instruction as not merely advisory but binding for the believer. The New Testament’s use of this term reflects God’s sovereign authority in issuing mandates that shape Christian conduct and belief. Recognizing these commands as παραγγελίαι reminds us that faith involves submission to God’s revealed will, entrusted through Scripture and apostolic teaching. This reinforces the call to obedience as an essential response to divine authority, rooted in the person and work of Christ who fulfills the law and issues His own commands to His followers.
keyVerseReflection: In Acts 5:28, the authorities say, 'Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name?' Here, παραγγελία underscores the strictness and official nature of the prohibition against teaching about Jesus. The word conveys the weight of the legal and authoritative charge that the apostles are accused of violating. This highlights the conflict between human authority and the divine mandate the apostles carry, reminding us that obedience to God’s commands surpasses human restrictions.
